bull_bear.body:
- Proprietary curriculum frameworks — the iCube Learning Ladder pedagogy at Shanti Juniors and a post-pandemic curriculum framework built through in-house R&D at Little Marvels
- Long-standing relationships with institution partners, global universities and parent communities, described as assets accumulated over 15 years of focused work
- Parentage of the Chiripal Group, which the company says gives institutional credibility and infrastructure support few education companies of its size can draw on
- Breadth of a six-brand portfolio spanning preschool, training, STEM, study-abroad counselling and uniforms, giving multiple revenue streams around one school ecosystem
- Distribution footprint: 350+ preschool centres across 74+ cities, described as an asset-light core model
- Licensed FranklinCovey Education training methodology at Catalyzer
- Keystone Global's representation network of 500+ global universities across 10 countries
- WSRO's robotics and STEM competition framework, with 25,000+ students trained since 2018 and a presence across 10 countries
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competitive intensity in preschool and K-12 education — The BRSR materiality table states that rising demand for quality education and rising Indian income levels have increased the number of preschools and K-12 schools, which in turn has added competition; a company that fails to innovate risks losing its competitive edge and customers as preferences evolve.
- Data privacy and cyber security — Identified as a material risk with negative financial implications. Malware, social engineering and software supply-chain attacks create a high risk of theft of sensitive customer data, which the company describes as both a data-privacy and a reputational risk. Mitigations cited are disk encryption, disablement of USB and a cyber security and data privacy policy; the Risk Management Committee reviews cyber security within the ERM framework.
- Human capital management and attrition — Identified as a material risk with negative financial implications. Low employee motivation is said to lead to decreased productivity, higher absenteeism, increased turnover, compromised work quality and reputational damage. The BRSR reports a permanent-employee turnover rate of 59% total in FY 2025-26 against 51% in FY 2024-25 and 14% in FY 2023-24, on a permanent employee base of 102 — attrition is structurally high and rising on a very small workforce.
- Single-activity and single-sector concentration — The BRSR reports that education services account for 100.00% of turnover, split between Education Support Service (38.43%) and Other Education (61.57%), with no exports (0.00% of turnover). Earnings depend entirely on one sector and on the domestic market.
- Geographic and footprint concentration — The BRSR reports operations in only 6 states nationally with zero plants and two offices, and no international locations, so the business is concentrated in a small number of Indian states even as the company aspires to reach every district headquarters.
- Franchisee- and partner-dependent operating model — The BRSR states that SEIL's customers include franchisees and that the company focuses on operations through franchisees for preschools, K-12 schools and higher studies, and that it does not have a direct workforce but engages workers through contracted services. Delivery quality, brand consistency and revenue therefore depend on third parties SEIL does not directly employ or control.
- Execution and approval risk on the proposed merger with GREW Energy — The Board-approved Scheme of Arrangement — slump sale of the education undertaking to Shanti Learning Initiatives Private Limited followed by amalgamation of SEIL with GREW Energy Private Limited — remains subject to approvals from shareholders, creditors, the Stock Exchanges, the jurisdictional NCLT and other regulators. Non-receipt or delay would leave shareholders holding a materially different asset than the one contemplated, and the transaction redirects SEIL shareholders' exposure from education to solar PV manufacturing.
- Compliance and disclosure timeliness under SEBI LODR — The Directors' Report records a Secretarial Audit observation beyond the standard clean position, with the Board assuring stakeholders that it is committed to robust compliance standards and has taken corrective measures to ensure timely submission of all future filings under SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 — implying a lapse in timely filing during the year.
- Business ethics and corporate governance — Listed by the company in its BRSR materiality table (as an opportunity) on the basis that non-compliance with business ethics often leads to significant reputational damage; managed through the Code of Conduct, whistleblower and related-party transaction policies. Separately, the Board states there are no risks which, in its opinion, threaten the existence of the Company.

business.body: SEIL provides strategic solutions for educational institutions from preschool to post-graduation, including the establishment and management of schools, curriculum and teacher training, educational technology, assessment, career counselling and institutional auxiliary services. It operates through six brands: Shanti Juniors and Little Marvels (preschools, largely franchisee-operated), Catalyzer (FranklinCovey Education licensed training and consultancy for individuals, schools and corporates), Keystone Global (study-abroad counselling and university representation), WSRO (robotics and STEM education and competitions) and UniformVerse (uniform manufacturing and multi-channel supply). Customers include franchisees, partner institutions and employed professionals, with the uniform business also serving corporate, healthcare, hospitality and sports clients beyond SEIL's own school network.

outlook.body:
- Strengthen and scale the existing six brands to increase reach and deepen market presence across India
- Diversify services to address gaps in the education system through new programmes and platforms
- Expand Catalyzer's consultancy and institutional training to a broader base of educational institutions and corporate clients
- Build a corporate learning and workforce-training business extending Catalyzer's capability-building mandate into the enterprise market
- Offer end-to-end school management solutions that simplify institutional operations and governance
- Launch online courses and certification programmes to extend curriculum and training beyond physical centres
- Offer dedicated career counselling and placement support for higher education institutions, building on Keystone Global's expertise
- Introduce a technology-enabled digital platform for uniform and accessories distribution under UniformVerse, building on the School Shack online store

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: SEIL's expansion is footprint- and platform-led rather than plant-led: the BRSR reports zero plants and two offices nationally, and the company describes an asset-light core with 350+ preschool centres across 74+ cities and an in-house uniform manufacturing facility. Stated forward initiatives are to strengthen and scale the six existing brands, expand Catalyzer's consultancy and institutional training to a broader base of institutions and corporate clients, build structured corporate learning and workforce-training programmes, provide end-to-end school management systems, launch an online courses and certification portfolio, offer career counselling and placement support for higher education institutions, and introduce a fully integrated technology-enabled distribution platform for uniforms and accessories under UniformVerse building on the School Shack online store. The company also states it will continue its push to establish a presence in every district headquarters in India, and lists integration of smart-classroom and digital learning technologies among its core focus areas. No timelines or rupee quantum are attached to any of these initiatives. Separately, on 2nd March 2026 the Boards approved a two-step Scheme of Arrangement: SEIL's business undertaking is transferred to Shanti Learning Initiatives Private Limited by slump sale, after which SEIL amalgamates with GREW Energy Private Limited (a Chiripal Group solar PV manufacturer operating a 6.5 GW module plant at Dudu, Rajasthan and setting up 8.0 GW of solar cells at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh, of which 3.0 GW are already operational), with GREW Energy to be listed on a recognised stock exchange upon all approvals. Those solar capacities belong to GREW Energy, the counterparty, not to SEIL. BRSR Principle 2 reports NIL R&D and NIL capex investments in technologies to improve environmental and social impacts in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management frames India as being on the cusp of an educational renaissance, with the world's largest youth population making education quality central to the national agenda
- The National Education Policy 2020 is described as driving reform by prioritising inclusivity, critical thinking and skill development, which management reads as an opportunity for well-positioned quality providers
- Digital learning platforms, AI-driven assessments and technology-enabled classrooms are reshaping teaching and learning, per management
- Management cites systemic under-penetration: although India hosts the world's third-largest higher education system, infrastructure gaps, teacher quality and inequitable funding leave quality education available to just 10% of the youth population — the space the company says it was built to address
- Rising demand for quality education and rising Indian income levels have increased the number of preschools and K-12 schools, which management notes has also added competition
- The company states the year's performance came despite tough economic conditions, that innovative and state-of-the-art technological measures were undertaken to drive efficiencies in preschool and K-12 school operations, and that it hopes for better performance in the current year

No timelines or rupee quantum are attached to any of these initiatives. Separately, on 2nd March 2026 the Boards approved a two-step Scheme of Arrangement: SEIL's business undertaking is transferred to Shanti Learning Initiatives Private Limited by slump sale, after which SEIL amalgamates with GREW Energy Private Limited (a Chiripal Group solar PV manufacturer operating a 6.5 GW module plant at Dudu, Rajasthan and setting up 8.0 GW of solar cells at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh, of which 3.0 GW are already operational), with GREW Energy to be listed on a recognised stock exchange upon all approvals. Those solar capacities belong to GREW Energy, the counterparty, not to SEIL. BRSR Principle 2 reports NIL R&D and NIL capex investments in technologies to improve environmental and social impacts in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Proprietary curriculum frameworks — the iCube Learning Ladder pedagogy at Shanti Juniors and a post-pandemic curriculum framework built through in-house R&D at Little Marvels
- Long-standing relationships with institution partners, global universities and parent communities, described as assets accumulated over 15 years of focused work
- Parentage of the Chiripal Group, which the company says gives institutional credibility and infrastructure support few education companies of its size can draw on
- Breadth of a six-brand portfolio spanning preschool, training, STEM, study-abroad counselling and uniforms, giving multiple revenue streams around one school ecosystem
- Distribution footprint: 350+ preschool centres across 74+ cities, described as an asset-light core model
- Licensed FranklinCovey Education training methodology at Catalyzer
- Keystone Global's representation network of 500+ global universities across 10 countries
- WSRO's robotics and STEM competition framework, with 25,000+ students trained since 2018 and a presence across 10 countries

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Competitive intensity in preschool and K-12 education — The BRSR materiality table states that rising demand for quality education and rising Indian income levels have increased the number of preschools and K-12 schools, which in turn has added competition; a company that fails to innovate risks losing its competitive edge and customers as preferences evolve.
- Data privacy and cyber security — Identified as a material risk with negative financial implications. Malware, social engineering and software supply-chain attacks create a high risk of theft of sensitive customer data, which the company describes as both a data-privacy and a reputational risk. Mitigations cited are disk encryption, disablement of USB and a cyber security and data privacy policy; the Risk Management Committee reviews cyber security within the ERM framework.
- Human capital management and attrition — Identified as a material risk with negative financial implications. Low employee motivation is said to lead to decreased productivity, higher absenteeism, increased turnover, compromised work quality and reputational damage. The BRSR reports a permanent-employee turnover rate of 59% total in FY 2025-26 against 51% in FY 2024-25 and 14% in FY 2023-24, on a permanent employee base of 102 — attrition is structurally high and rising on a very small workforce.
- Single-activity and single-sector concentration — The BRSR reports that education services account for 100.00% of turnover, split between Education Support Service (38.43%) and Other Education (61.57%), with no exports (0.00% of turnover). Earnings depend entirely on one sector and on the domestic market.
- Geographic and footprint concentration — The BRSR reports operations in only 6 states nationally with zero plants and two offices, and no international locations, so the business is concentrated in a small number of Indian states even as the company aspires to reach every district headquarters.
- Franchisee- and partner-dependent operating model — The BRSR states that SEIL's customers include franchisees and that the company focuses on operations through franchisees for preschools, K-12 schools and higher studies, and that it does not have a direct workforce but engages workers through contracted services. Delivery quality, brand consistency and revenue therefore depend on third parties SEIL does not directly employ or control.
- Execution and approval risk on the proposed merger with GREW Energy — The Board-approved Scheme of Arrangement — slump sale of the education undertaking to Shanti Learning Initiatives Private Limited followed by amalgamation of SEIL with GREW Energy Private Limited — remains subject to approvals from shareholders, creditors, the Stock Exchanges, the jurisdictional NCLT and other regulators. Non-receipt or delay would leave shareholders holding a materially different asset than the one contemplated, and the transaction redirects SEIL shareholders' exposure from education to solar PV manufacturing.
- Compliance and disclosure timeliness under SEBI LODR — The Directors' Report records a Secretarial Audit observation beyond the standard clean position, with the Board assuring stakeholders that it is committed to robust compliance standards and has taken corrective measures to ensure timely submission of all future filings under SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 — implying a lapse in timely filing during the year.
- Business ethics and corporate governance — Listed by the company in its BRSR materiality table (as an opportunity) on the basis that non-compliance with business ethics often leads to significant reputational damage; managed through the Code of Conduct, whistleblower and related-party transaction policies. Separately, the Board states there are no risks which, in its opinion, threaten the existence of the Company.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen and scale the existing six brands to increase reach and deepen market presence across India
- Diversify services to address gaps in the education system through new programmes and platforms
- Expand Catalyzer's consultancy and institutional training to a broader base of educational institutions and corporate clients
- Build a corporate learning and workforce-training business extending Catalyzer's capability-building mandate into the enterprise market
- Offer end-to-end school management solutions that simplify institutional operations and governance
- Launch online courses and certification …
